clue.text: Financier having 100 for northern supporter

indicators.note: having one thing for another signals a swap of letters in the word for financier
for here means in place of, marking which letter the new one replaces

parts.note: a banker is a financier
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A money man swaps a northern backer for a hundred, as if trading investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having 100 for northern' puts C (Roman 100) in place of the N in BANKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer is someone who funds or champions a venture, a synonym for supporter.

clue.text: I must replace what's at heart of bad offer

indicators.note: must replace tells us a letter is swapped out for the letter I in the word bad
the heart of a three-letter word is its middle letter, the one being swapped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction: put I in the middle of a bad offer to improve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's at heart of bad' is A, the middle letter, and 'I must replace' it, giving B-I-D.
explanation.definitionFit: A bid is an offer of a price, as at an auction.

clue.text: Talk about milliner

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a milliner makes hats, so is a hatter

explanation.surface: A conversation concerning a hat-maker, perhaps the Mad Hatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives C (circa), not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is idle talk, a synonym used as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Men bash titles for representing upper echelon

indicators.note: representing means depicting in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men attacking titles stand for an attack on the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the ruling elite of a society, its top tier.

clue.text: Priest perhaps given lodging by Uncle Richard

indicators.note: something lodged in other words is housed inside them, so the answer sits within uncle Richard

explanation.surface: A clergyman staying with a relative named Richard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given lodging by' places the answer across 'unCLE RICHard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is one example of a cleric, a member of the clergy; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Like Hals' cavalier with reputation as an object of ridicule

parts.note: The Laughing Cavalier is the famous portrait by Frans Hals
stock can mean standing or reputation, as in one's stock rising

explanation.surface: A painting's subject whose fame has made him a figure of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Laughing Cavalier is a 1624 portrait by the Dutch painter Frans Hals, held in London's Wallace Collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A laughingstock is a person everybody mocks, exactly an object of ridicule.

clue.text: Dangerous creature runs round outside hotel and inside

indicators.note: outside here means the round letter goes on the outer end, after the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
inside means in
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dangerous beast charges round a hotel, outside and in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is O, put 'outside', i.e. at the end, after R, H and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros, shortened to rhino, is a large animal known to charge.

clue.text: Addictive form of cocaine reduced in repressive measure

parts.note: crack is a smokable form of cocaine
down means lowered or reduced, as in prices being down

explanation.surface: Police clamp down on crack cocaine, reducing its spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a severe official clampdown, a repressive measure.

clue.text: Rough sketch of simple boat on delta

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the boat comes after delta

parts.note: D is Delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a raft is a basic flat boat

explanation.surface: A quick drawing of a raft on a river delta.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a rough sketch.

clue.text: Reformed lamina including uranium metal oxide

indicators.note: including means holding the uranium letter within the rearranged lamina
reformed means shaped anew, so the letters of lamina are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A thin layer re-formed with uranium yields a chemical compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' turns LAMINA into ALMINA; 'including' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumina is aluminium oxide, a compound of a metal with oxygen.

clue.text: An object to touch

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Being asked to object to being touched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' is a noun here: a but, as in 'no buts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut meet at an edge, so they touch each other.

clue.text: Formal agreement dropping the first parliamentary statute

indicators.note: dropping the first means the opening letter of the word for formal agreement is removed

parts.note: a pact is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A treaty loses its opening clause to become a law.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act of Parliament is a law passed by the legislature, a statute.

clue.text: Change outside of one meteorological flight instrument

indicators.note: outside of means the word for change wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to alter is to change
I is the Roman numeral for one
Met is short for meteorological, as in the Met Office

explanation.surface: Altering the outside of a weather-measuring device for aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' is the containment signal: the word for change wraps around one and the Met Office short form, so 'meteorological' is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter measures an aircraft's height, a key cockpit instrument.

clue.text: Painter's way of working with black to speed up task

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to rush is to hurry
work is a task to be done

explanation.surface: An artist's method involves dark paint and hurrying through a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushwork is the characteristic way an artist applies paint with a brush.

clue.text: Turned over furrow to pinch root vegetable

indicators.note: turned over means the word for furrow is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow
to nip is to pinch

explanation.surface: A ploughed furrow used to steal a root crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reverses RUT to TUR; 'pinch' is NIP, not steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a round white root eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: In diamonds I go for blue colour

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player announces they will bid in diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet dye and shade.

clue.text: Occupy one new hospital a little at a time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a bit is a little, taken here bit by bit

explanation.surface: Moving into a new hospital gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in it, a synonym for occupy.

clue.text: Take a gamble importing European root crop

indicators.note: importing means bringing the European letter into the word for gamble

parts.note: to bet is to take a gamble

explanation.surface: Speculating by bringing in a foreign vegetable crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Beet, grown for sugar or as beetroot, is a crop harvested for its root.

clue.text: Mass at church with the French saint is without equal

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Mass in a French saint's church is unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks religious but is the physics M.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means having no match or rival, so peerless.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: a hearing of a case in court

explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both a court hearing of evidence and an experiment testing something.

clue.text: Chicken when headless

indicators.note: headless means the word when loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Calls to mind a chicken running about with its head cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female chicken.

clue.text: Make division time stand up before court

parts.note: to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: A judge orders everyone to rise before a court session divides.
explanation.definitionFit: To trisect is to cut into three equal parts, a kind of division.

clue.text: Circulate gold piece

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Passing a gold coin around.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to travel round and round something, to circle it.

clue.text: What can protect wood in burnt arboretum.

indicators.note: in signals the answer is found inside the run of letters burnt arboretum

explanation.surface: Asks what might preserve trees in a fire-damaged arboretum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is a black coating painted on timber, fences and boats to preserve them.

clue.text: Tell Romeo story in reverse, with end at the start

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in reverse means the word for story is read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of the word end is taken

explanation.surface: Telling Romeo's story backwards, starting from the tragic ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns TALE into ELAT; 'end at the start' is the first letter of 'end', E, not an instruction to move letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or recount it.

clue.text: Backed exams taken again eliminating English winter sportsperson

indicators.note: eliminating means the English letter is removed from the reversed word
backed means the word for exams taken again is read in reverse

parts.note: retakes are exams sat a second time

explanation.surface: Repeating exams instead of going skiing or skating this winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' turns RETAKES into SEKATER; 'eliminating English' removes an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater glides on ice, a classic winter sport.
